links.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of LLM patient-level responses on FHA
links.effect: Median FRES was 43.5 (IQR 36.8-53.4) for Gemini, 30.6 (16.8-48.4) for ChatGPT 3.5, and 28.8 (22.1-37.6) for ChatGPT 4.0; lower scores indicate more difficult reading.
links.quote: Readability differed significantly among models (p = 0.012), with Gemini producing the most readable patient-level content (median FRES 43.5 [IQR 36.8-53.4]) compared with ChatGPT 3.5 (30.6 [16.8-48.4]) and ChatGPT 4.0 (28.8 [22.1-37.6]).

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient-directed answers measured by FRES
links.effect: All models had median FRES below 50 (28.8-43.5), indicating difficult reading; Gemini most readable, differences significant (p = 0.012).
links.quote: Readability differed significantly among models (p = 0.012), with Gemini producing the most readable patient-level content (median FRES 43.5 [IQR 36.8-53.4]) compared with ChatGPT 3.5 (30.6 [16.8-48.4]) and ChatGPT 4.0 (28.8 [22.1-37.6]).

links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM answers to FHA questions versus expert ratings
links.effect: Patient-level accuracy: ChatGPT 4.0 9/11 (82%), ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini 8/11 (73%). Clinician-level: OpenEvidence 15/15 (100%), ChatGPT 4.0 93%, Gemini 80%.
links.quote: Among clinician-level questions, OpenEvidence demonstrated perfect accuracy (15 of 15; 100%), compared with 93% for and 80% for ChatGPT 4.0 and Gemini.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning on field-specific data and engineered prompts to improve LLM accuracy
Comparing general-purpose LLMs with evidence-retrieval LLM (OpenEvidence) for clinician questions

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, completeness, and readability of four commercial LLMs on patient-level and clinician-level questions about functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
